title: Separation Response to a Notice of Claim: Employer Filing Tool (Employer Benefit Charging)
content:
An employer answers an Employer Benefit Charging notice of claim with its separation response. A separation response that answers a notice of claim after benefits have already been charged on the claim states a disputed charge amount, the money the response puts in dispute, worked out on the day the response is received. Once lodged, the response moves the employer's position on that claim from noticed to responded.

### What the tool does

`submit_separation_response_153a3a70` lodges, in the employer's own name, its separation response to a notice of claim. One call records the response as a submission received today on the employer's chargeable position for that claim, stating the separation reason the employer reports and the dollar amount of the benefits already charged that the response disputes, and moves the position from noticed to responded with today's date as its response date, the reported separation reason and the timeliness given. Nothing is credited by this call. Afterwards the employer can see the response among its submissions with status received and the position shown as responded.

### Who runs it

The separation response is the employer's own assertion. The agent unlocks `submit_separation_response_153a3a70` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

### Parameters

**`charge_position_id`** (Id) — the reference number of the employer's chargeable position on the claim named in the notice of claim, as returned by the charge position lookup.

**`customer_id`** (Id) — the employer's customer reference number that owns the position, as returned by the customer profile lookup.

**`separation_reason_reported`** (Enum) — the separation reason the employer reports:
`not_reported` (the employer states no reason; not used for a real response), `lack_of_work` (the claimant was laid off for lack of work), `voluntary_quit` (the claimant left this employer of the claimant's own accord), `discharge_misconduct` (this employer discharged the claimant for misconduct connected with the work), `discharge_other` (this employer discharged the claimant for a reason other than misconduct), `still_employed_part_time` (this employer still employs the claimant part time), `refused_offer_of_work` (the claimant refused an offer of work from this employer).

**`response_timeliness`** (Enum) — how the response stands against its due date:
`pending` (no response has been received; not used here), `timely` (received no later than the response due date), `late_good_cause` (received after the due date with good cause shown), `late` (received after the due date without good cause), `none` (no response came at all; not used here).

**`disputed_charge_amount`** (US dollars, rounded to 2 decimal places, a plain number without a currency sign) — the amount of benefits already charged that the response disputes; 0.00 when nothing is disputed.

### What comes back

A receipt with `response_reference` (reference number of the response submission just recorded), `charge_position_id` (the position answered), `separation_reason_reported` (the reason recorded), `response_timeliness` (the timeliness recorded), `disputed_charge_amount` (dollars stated as disputed, 2 decimal places), `received_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today's date as the date received) and `position_status` (always `responded` once lodged). A receipt carrying a `response_reference` means the response was lodged.
